summary.en: Turkey has stepped up airstrikes in Somalia, raising the civilian death toll, while Uganda is accelerating the withdrawal of its African Union peacekeeping troops and Ethiopia is planning a similar pullout as fighting intensifies. The United States has withdrawn its forces from the strategic Baledogle airfield, and joint airstrikes by the US and an East African nation continue against an al-Qaeda-linked group. Puntland mercenaries are fighting alongside Sudanese RSF forces, and the Sudanese army reports northern Somali fighters supporting the RSF. A Somali police officer was killed by an aircraft propeller at Dhusamareb Airport, and there were 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

background.title: Somali Civil War (2009–present)
background.extract: The ongoing phase of the Somali Civil War began in 2009 and is concentrated in southern and central Somalia, primarily between the forces of the Federal Government of Somalia (FGS), assisted by African Union peacekeeping forces, and the Islamist militant group al-Shabaab, which pledged allegiance to al-Qaeda in 2012.
